title: Per-endpoint SLO bands, SLI attribution, and adaptive failover guardrails
creator: Maya Patel
description: Define a canonical, actionable spec for per-endpoint SLO bands (quality/latency/availability), a deterministic SLI attribution model for mixed-quality routes (chat vs. generation vs. embeddings), and an adaptive failover + circuit breaker policy that ties to error-budget burn rates. This ticket produces the policy doc, telemetry requirements, and a rollout plan for automated region-level failover and graceful degradation across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: A1: SLO band definitions (Platinum/Gold/Silver/Bronze) published with clear numeric SLI thresholds for latency, availability, and correctness QoR for each route type.

A2: SLI attribution model implemented in telemetry (per-request labels: route, model_variant, tenant_priority, region, request_size) and validated against 7 days of production traffic in 'slo-shadow' mode.

A3: Error budget burn-rate policy defined with automated actions: alerting (2x burn), throttling(5x), soft-shedding(10x), circuit-breaker activation(20x), and region failover condition (sustained 15x for 5m + availability drop).
A4: Circuit breaker logic implemented in routing layer with config knobs (RT percentile thresholds, queue depth, GPU stall metrics) and unit+integration tests.
A5: Chaos test that simulates a regional instance spike causes failover within expected window, and post-failover rollback path restores traffic when metrics recover.
notes_and_decisions: Decision: Use a four-band SLO taxonomy (Platinum/Gold/Silver/Bronze) to balance simplicity and flexibility; teams can map routes to bands rather than author bespoke SLOs per endpoint.

Decision: SLIs will be a small set of canonical metrics: p99 latency (ms), successful request rate (>=200/stream end), and a route-specific quality SLI (for chat/generation this is pass/fail on a small promptset eval sampled in-prod).
Trade-off: Per-tenant SLOs are in scope later; initial rollout will be per-endpoint/per-model-variant with tenant-priority tagging to enable future billing/contracting work.
Telemetry note: We'll add an "sli_bucket" tag to traces and metrics to enable efficient aggregation for multiple rollups and to avoid cardinality explosion.

Fallback policy: When error budget burn > 10x, prefer soft degradation (lower-cost model variant -> quantized variant) before hard dropping requests; hard drops only for safety (queue length, GPU OOM risk).
Observability: Traffic-level dashboards (per-route, per-variant) and a synthesized 'Error Budget Health' view are required before enabling auto-failover.
plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Draft SLO band spec, SLI mapping table, and telemetry schema changes. Deliverables: spec doc + metric names + tagging plan.
Phase 2 (3 weeks): Implement SLI attribution in collector (add request labels, sample evaluation pipeline for quality SLI), add alerts for burn-rate thresholds.
Phase 3 (3 weeks): Implement routing layer circuit breaker and soft-shedding policy. Expose runtime knobs in Console (failover thresholds, knob overrides per-tenant).
Phase 4 (2 weeks): Integrate multi-region failover orchestrator: detection rules, cooldown, and rollback. Run staged canary in non-prod, then shadow in prod for 7 days.
Phase 5 (1 week): Run chaos experiments, document runbook, train on-call, and flip auto-failover to opt-in for two pilot customers.
Post-rollout: Iterate on per-tenant SLO support and add SLA contract linking for enterprise customers.
telemetry_requirements: Add tags: route_id, model_variant, tenant_id (nullable), priority_tier, region, request_tokens, response_tokens.
Histogram metrics for latency (p50/p90/p95/p99) and tail quantiles for token-latency on streamed responses.
Synthetic quality probes: For conversational routes, sample 0.5% of requests to run lightweight promptset checks (store pass/fail counter per-route).
Expose an error-budget ledger per SLO band with 30/7/1 day burn-rate windows.
Implement a fast aggregation pipeline for the 'Error Budget Health' view (sub-minute rollups).
failover_and_circuit_breaker_spec: Trigger conditions (region-level): sustained p99 latency > 2x baseline OR availability < 99% for 5m AND error budget burn-rate >= 15 for 5m.
Circuit-breaker scopes: per-model-variant, per-route, per-region. Activation levels: warn -> soft-shed -> hard-shed -> route-circuit-open.
Soft-shedding strategy: step down to pre-configured lower-cost model_variant (quantized / smaller size) and reduce batch sizes; continue accepting requests but at degraded quality.
Hard-shedding strategy: reject low-priority requests (tenant priority) and serve 503 with structured JSON explaining degradation path; route critical requests to fallback model in other region.
Cooldown/Recovery: when metrics return below thresholds for a sustained window (3x SLO window), allow gradual re-add (linear ramp) of traffic to original region/variant.
Rate of rollback: exponential backoff on re-enable attempts to avoid oscillation across regions.
Safety limits: never failover more than 40% of global traffic to a single region without manual approval during business hours.
observability_and_alerting: Dashboards: per-route SLO burn, per-variant health, region availability, and a synthetic 'failover score' indicator.
Alerts: pager on severe (>20x burn or sustained availability <95% for 5m), Slack -ops for >5x burn, and email to PM/SE for persistent degradation.

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Cardinality explosion from per-request labels. Mitigation: use cardinality caps and only record tenant_id for high-value routes; implement sampling for low-traffic routes.
Risk: Oscillation (flip-flopping) between regions during borderline incidents. Mitigation: additive cooldowns, progressive ramp, and global safety guard (40% traffic cap).
Risk: Quality regressions when stepping down models. Mitigation: pre-computed quality profiles per-variant and a pre-registered fallback matrix tested in staging.
